title: D-reviewhint: review packets name the real diff command and base, and the diff budget honours [limits].review_diff_chars
spec:
Goal T-1403, plan label D-reviewhint (added by the human 2026-10-02 'do those'). Evidence from today: reviews T-1573, T-1574 (of T-1569) and T-1579 (of T-1578) each returned request_changes 'the scoped diff was unavailable' without reading code; T-1579's comments then made the daemon file a useless fix round (T-1580, cancelled). Three causes in orchestrator/spawn.py review_packet (locate by symbol):
(a) The expand hint is `git -C {wt} diff -- {scope}`: a working-tree diff with no revision range, which prints nothing once the work is committed. scoped_diff(src) itself runs `git diff -U3 {base}...HEAD -- {scope}` with base = goal/<parent> when that branch exists else origin/main; the hint must be that same command: `git -C {wt} diff -U3 {base}...HEAD -- {scope}` with the same base resolution (factor the base choice into one helper used by both, e.g. scoped_diff_base(src)).
(b) diff_budget = max(1, min(configured_cap, 8000 - other_chars - diff_heading_chars)): the 8000 constant means [limits].review_diff_chars (live value 12000) never applies and a 24k-char diff reaches the reviewer as ~7k chars plus a marker. Change: diff_budget = max(1, configured_cap) where configured_cap = cfg['limits'].get('review_diff_chars', 12000); the other sections are not subtracted (they are small and already bounded by bounded_text where used). The spec_review packet keeps its own spec_review_code_chars budget unchanged.
(c) _base_sha(task, worktree) returns the worktree HEAD (short sha) and the packet presents it as the base, so reviewers of a fix round that committed on its parent's branch read 'base = <HEAD>' and conclude there is nothing to diff (T-1574 said exactly that). Change: _base_sha returns the short sha of `git merge-base {base} HEAD` in the worktree (base from the helper in (a)), '(unavailable)' on failure; the packet line that shows it is labelled as the diff base, and a new line names the branch under review: the task's recorded branch (task['branch']) when set, else task/<id>, with the HEAD short sha.
Keep: bounded_diff's marker format, the evidence candidates built from raw_diff, every other packet section.

Tests (SPEC RULE): tests/test_spawn.py has test_bounded_diff_expansion_hint and a packet-size assertion near 'review_diff_chars' (grep) that bounds the prompt by review_diff_chars + 2000: keep it passing (if the new budget makes it fail, bound it by review_diff_chars + the length of the non-diff sections + 64 and say so). Add the acceptance tests below as unittest.TestCase methods using tests/_harness.py like the neighbouring packet tests (they build a scratch repo with a goal branch, a task worktree with one commit beyond it, and call spawn.review_packet with a small cfg). Run tests/test_spawn.py in the foreground after committing; never background a command and never run the full gate.

Out of scope: daemon.py, failures.py, prompts, bus.py. Rollback: git revert of the merge commit.

Work on the task branch cut from goal/T-1403. Commit first, then run the focused tests in the foreground. Locate every insertion point by symbol, never by line number. Every test named in the acceptance must exist in the diff; the gate checks for them by id.
acceptance: tests/test_spawn.py::test_review_packet_hint_names_base_range_and_branch: passes: for a task whose worktree has one commit beyond goal/<parent>, review_packet's expand hint is exactly the scoped_diff command with the goal base (`git -C <wt> diff -U3 goal/<parent>...HEAD -- <scope>`), the packet's base line shows the merge-base short sha (not HEAD), and the packet names the branch under review (task['branch'] when set, else task/<id>) with the HEAD short sha; with no goal branch the hint and base use origin/main

tests/test_spawn.py::test_review_packet_diff_budget_honours_review_diff_chars: passes: with [limits].review_diff_chars 20000 and a scoped diff of 15000 chars, the packet contains the whole diff and no 'more lines' marker; with review_diff_chars 3000 the diff section is cut with the marker and the hint from the first test; the packet never cuts the diff at 8000 when the configured value is larger
